generation_settings.duration_note: All our prompts are written with timestamped beats (0.0-1.5s, 1.5-3.0s, etc) that assume an 8-second clip. If Flow only offers 4/6/8s options, always pick 8 — shorter durations will cut a beat off mid-motion.
generation_settings.mode: single start image + text motion prompt (image-to-video), NOT a start+end frame pair
generation_settings.mode_note: Do not assume this matches whatever mode a generic doc calls 'Frames to Video' (that implies both start AND end images, and historically ran far more expensive per generation than what we've actually paid). Before running step 6 of the test, use browser_snapshot to confirm which mode in the real Flow UI takes ONE image + text prompt, and check the actual credit cost shown before generating — don't assume, verify live.
generation_settings.quality_tier: start on the cheapest/fastest available tier to validate the pipeline (chaining, frame extraction, browser automation) works end-to-end without burning credits on quality. Only switch to the top-quality tier once a segment's composition and motion are already approved at low quality — quality tier doesn't change whether the prompt/motion/chaining logic works, only sharpness.
generation_settings.audio: off if there's a toggle — we mute all AI-generated audio and add our own sound/music in CapCut, per the video_tail below
generation_settings.image_tool: Nano Banana Pro for every start-image generation, always generate 4 variants and stop — show all 4 to the user and let them pick which one to animate. Never auto-pick a variant yourself.
generation_settings.video_tool: Omni, within Google Flow, for every video/motion generation, at the 8-second duration set above.

format: 9:16 vertical, photorealistic editorial still base, 50mm shallow depth of field
lighting: hard directional key light from one side, deep near-black shadows, strong specular highlights, high contrast, never flat, never evenly lit
image_tail: Photorealistic, editorial still, shot on 50mm, shallow depth of field, 9:16 vertical. Hard directional key light from one side, deep near-black shadows, strong specular highlights. Palette: near-black navy #0F1E30 background, warm cream #E8DED1, one saturated rust-red #C4533F accent. High contrast, not flat, not evenly lit. No text anywhere in frame, no captions, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no watermark, no readable documents, no visible faces, no house numbers, no street signs.
video_tail: Camera behaviour as stated above - do not default to a fully static locked-off shot for the whole duration. Pick exactly ONE camera movement type for this shot (push, whip-pan, rack-focus, drift, tilt, or crash zoom) - never stack two movements in the same shot (e.g. never 'push in while panning'), that reliably produces jarring or unpredictable motion. Vary WHICH single movement you pick across different shots/segments, not within one. Motion begins decisively or violently on the very first frame, never a calm intro. AUDIO: ambient only, no music, no dialogue, no voiceover. No text appears at any point, no captions, no subtitles, no logos, no watermark, no visible faces.
narrative_sections: 1. Цена ошибки — concrete cost, money/documents (no readable currency or text — see known-failures.md)
2. Скрытое под поверхностью — walls, cracks, damp, hidden defects
3. Два варианта — side-by-side comparison, contrast in light not narration
4. Время и будущие счета — decay, deadlines, hourglass-type imagery
5. Разрушение — bold destructive reveal (material tears/bursts open, not camera phasing through solid matter)
6. Разрешение и зелёный флаг — calm resolution, warm light, contrast payoff after tension
reliable_techniques: large-scale weather transformation (rain to snow to sun, storm clears)
light/color wave sweeping across a surface (cold to warm, red to green)
cascading ignition (windows, streetlamps, candles lighting one after another)
avalanche/collapse of a large stacked object (coins, cards, papers)
material bursting/tearing open explosively to reveal what's behind (roof, wall, ceiling) — the MATERIAL destroys itself, the camera does not pass through solid matter
hard flash-cut between two states (storm to sunny, dark to lit) — write it as an explicit instant cut, not a dissolve
camera flying through an already-open gap into revealed space — only after the barrier is removed, never through something still solid
